title: Three Straight Axes: The Gantry, the Time of a Straight Line Across Axes of Different Strength, and What a Long Beam Does to Accuracy

questions.question: Why does a gantry need no inverse kinematics?
options: Its controller solves it in hardware
Each axis has its own encoder
It only ever moves one axis at a time
The tool's place is the axes' positions
questions.explanation: x, y and z are each one slide. The tool is where the slides are, with nothing to solve.

questions.question: Which took longer for the move of 0.4 m and 0.4 m?
options: A straight line, 0.900 s
Each axis on its own, 0.900 s
They took the same, 0.825 s
A straight line, 1.650 s
questions.explanation: On a line every axis must keep its share, so the slowest axis in speed and the slowest in acceleration both limit the path. Here those were different axes, and the line took longer.

questions.question: Twice the span made the sag how many times as great?
options: 2 times
4 times
16 times
questions.explanation: The sag of a beam loaded in the middle goes as the cube of its length, and two cubed is eight.

questions.question: The first resonance for 5 kg was:
options: 71 Hz
7.1 Hz
710 Hz
50 Hz, the mains
questions.explanation: A stiffness of 1.0 MN/m and 5 kg: the root of 200000 is 447 rad/s, which is 71 Hz. A heavier head lowers it.

questions.question: What does a skew of the two ends give?
options: A sag in the middle of the beam
An error that grows with the lever, from the beam turning
A lower resonance
An error that is the same everywhere on the beam
questions.explanation: The beam turns by the skew over the span, and a tool out on a lever moves by that angle times the lever: 0.2 mm over 1.0 m gave 60 micrometres at 0.3 m.

questions.question: What makes a bigger gantry less accurate?
options: Its motors, which lose steps on long travels
Its belts, which stretch in proportion to length
Its encoders, whose error adds along the travel
Its beams, whose sag grows with the cube of the length unless the section grows
questions.explanation: Doubling a span with the same section makes the sag eight times as great. The section has to grow with the length to keep the accuracy.
